title: [observability] 145.sh judges only a quiet round of its sweep: unreadable processes that come and go (gpg-agent, non-dumpable) are retried for up to 120 s, then an exit 2, never a false failure
prompt:
Spawn, objective 236 [observability] (the lead's ask of 2026-11-19 18:2x from rev-g's root cause sync/flaky/145.md; owner part only, no src; author rev-g; readers rev-b first, rev-e second, who writes ready/236): 145.sh judges only a quiet round of its sweep, so unreadable processes that come and go no longer fail it.

Why. 145.sh (the sweep of landed build output, objective 145) failed once on a head that does not touch the sweep (rev-g's 232 proof r1, 14:56): three rounds of (3), each hit by a gpg-agent starting or ending, and the third judged whatever it saw.
- gpg-agent makes itself non-dumpable: even the long-running agent, the same uid and the same pid namespace, has an unreadable /proc cwd and maps. The sweep's in-use proof can never clear it and rightly calls such a process "in use unknown".
- The 16 backup scenarios each start one in their scratch GNUPGHOME for their run, and kill it at cleanup. A read-only 15-minute watch saw 14 come and go, about one a minute on a busy host.
- `gpg --no-autostart --symmetric` fails on GnuPG 2.4.4, so the agents cannot be avoided at gpg.
- 145.sh (3) says "three times at most, and only a round that saw no new unreadable process is judged", but every retry branch stops at round 3, so the third round is judged whatever it saw. And a reviewed list refused for an excused process that has ended is a check failure there, not a retry.
- The sweep was right every time. The test's assumption, that three back-to-back rounds of 1-2 s find a quiet host, is what fails.

What changes (owner part, rsi/scenarios/145.sh (3) only; every assertion on the judged round unchanged):
- A round is quiet when the reviewed list and --apply saw exactly the unreadable set the list named:
  - the reviewed list exits 0 and names no unreadable process;
  - and --apply is not refused for "is not the one read" or for an excuse whose process ended.
- A reviewed list refused for an excuse whose process ended is a round that was not quiet, not a failure.
- An unreadable process that starts during --apply, after its first look, is met only when it judges a path again just before removing it, and shows only as `stays <path> <who>: in use unknown: process N (comm) of its owner cannot be read` (R2: rev-b's F1; one present at the first look changes the digest and is refused as above). A path kept for any other reason is still judged. With nothing removed, the round was not quiet and is tried again. With a path already removed, the planted scratch is gone, so 145.sh exits 2, run again (the proof met this once: a transient unreadable `spawn` process of another session).
- A round that was not quiet is tried again after 2 s, for SPAWN_145_QUIET_SECS (default 120) in all. Only the quiet round is judged.
- With no quiet round by then, 145.sh exits 2 (harness): "(3) no quiet round in <n> s (<rounds> rounds; the last: <why>): unreadable processes of this user kept coming (gpg-agent is non-dumpable); run again". Never 1.
  - The gate counts an exit 2 as no vote: cannot_judge, judged again after its backoff, never accepted on it; on the base, host_fault.
  - So the fallback is an honest "cannot judge", not a pass and not a candidate failure.
- No sweep change. Excusing gpg-agent by name is refused on purpose: a name is no proof, and "in use unknown" is the sweep's safety property.

Files: rsi/scenarios/145.sh, rsi/scenarios/236.sh (new), rsi/backlog/236.json (new).

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/236.sh, black box. It runs the tree's own 145.sh with SPAWN_BIN a wrapper around the binary under test that changes no argument and no output. From the call after 145.sh's (4) refused excuse (--excuse <pid>:1) on, before each of the next N `scratch sweep` calls, the wrapper kills the gpg-agent it started last and starts a fresh one (gpg-connect-agent in a scratch GNUPGHOME of its own): real churn of unreadable processes of this user.
- (0) the agent the wrapper starts is unreadable here (its /proc cwd); else a harness exit 2.
- (1) churn over the next 6 sweep calls, then none: 145.sh exits 0, three runs in a row, and its first (3) round was not judged. If 145.sh itself says run again (exit 2), 236.sh exits 2 too, never 1.
- (2) churn on every sweep call with SPAWN_145_QUIET_SECS=10: 145.sh exits 2, never 1, says "no quiet round" and "run again", and takes under 90 s;
- (3) (R2, rev-b's F2) an agent killed and started only before each of the first 3 --apply calls: the list changed, then an excused process ended; 145.sh exits 0;
- (4) (R2, rev-b's F2) an agent added, none killed, before each of the first 3 reviewed lists: an unreadable process started since the list; 145.sh exits 0.
On main 2e145e90, 236.sh exits 1: (3)'s reviewed list fails on an excused agent that ended. 145.sh as changed passes on its own, as before.

Verified by: after landing, 145.sh's runs in gates and proofs show no exit 1 from (3) caused by an unreadable process (the lead's gate table; rev-g's look over a week).
